messages.subject: problems with lognormal
parts:
Hi all,
I am trying to estimate the parameters of two lognormal variables, Y0 and Y1.
Y1 is shifted by tau. In R they are generated like this:

Y0 <- rlnorm( N, 0, 1 )
Y1<- Y0 + tau

where tau is 1.

This is my code in stan:

data {
  int<lower=0> N0;             
  vector<lower=0>[N0] y0;               
  int<lower=0> N1;             
  vector[N1] y1;              
}

transformed data {
  real min_y1;
  min_y1 <- min(y1);
}
parameters {
  real<lower=0,upper=10>sigma;             
  real                     mu;
  real<lower=if_else(min_y1>=0, 0, min_y1),upper=if_else(min_y1>=0,min_y1, 0)> tau;
}


model {
log(y0)~normal(mu, sigma);
log(y1-tau)~normal(mu, sigma);
}

The problem is that mu is always overestimated and tau is always underestimated. Any ideas?

Thank you

Laura

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] problems with lognormal
parts:
1) Tau is definitely not limited by the empirical bounds, which are random variables.
2) Use the lognormal directly.
3) Priors may help.  In particular, avoid hard constraints unless they’re physical
(i.e. lower=0 in sigma is good, but the upper=10 is not).

Try

data {
  int<lower=0> N0;             
  vector<lower=0>[N0] y0;               
  int<lower=0> N1;             
  vector[N1] y1;              
}

parameters {
  real<lower=0> sigma;             
  real mu;
  real  tau;
}

model {
sigma ~ cauchy(0, 2.5);
tau ~ normal(0, 10);

y0 ~ lognormal(mu, sigma);
y1 ~ lognormal(mu + tau, sigma);
}

If you know that tau is always positive then you can define it with a lower=0
bound and switch the normal prior to a half-Cauchy prior.
